name: identity_resilience_array
label: The Shard-Core Interface
godotFeature: SubViewportContainer (for dynamic UI rendering) combined with Control nodes, custom ShaderMaterials, and InputEvent handling for real-time interaction.
poeticVision: The player's very self-hood is laid bare on the screen—not as abstract bars, but as tangible shards orbiting a fading core. As the Silence hunts Lyra, these memories writhe, attempting to escape her grasp, pulled by unseen currents. The player feels a constant, desperate tug-of-war in real-time, struggling to anchor their fading identity while simultaneously fighting for physical survival. It's the visceral grief of self-loss made interactive, a direct measure of what slips away with every passing moment of danger.
usage: Attach this `identity_resilience_array.gd` script to a `Control` node. This `Control` node should be a child of a `SubViewportContainer` within your UI scene. The `SubViewportContainer` will render this dynamic identity interface. External game logic (e.g., player takes damage, Silence entity is near, Lyra loses a memory) should call `add_stress(amount: float)` on this `Control` node to increase the overall stress level, causing shards to drift. Players interact by clicking on drifting shards to 'anchor' them, preventing their loss. Listen to the `shard_lost` and `shard_anchored` signals to implement game consequences (e.g., skill degradation, buffs/debuffs). Ensure `shard_material.gdshader` is created in `res://`.

parameters.name: core_texture
parameters.description: The texture for the central identity core.

parameters.name: shard_texture
parameters.description: The texture for individual memory shards.

parameters.name: num_shards
parameters.description: The number of memory shards representing Lyra's identity.

parameters.name: base_orbit_radius
parameters.description: The initial distance of shards from the core.

parameters.name: orbit_speed
parameters.description: The speed at which shards orbit the core.

parameters.name: stress_drift_multiplier
parameters.description: How much the current stress level influences the shard's outward drift speed.

parameters.name: max_shard_drift
parameters.description: The maximum distance a shard can drift from its base orbit before being permanently lost.

parameters.name: anchor_duration
parameters.description: The duration (in seconds) a shard remains 'anchored' after a successful player interaction, during which its drift is paused/reduced.

parameters.name: shard_size
parameters.description: The size of the TextureRect nodes used for individual memory shards.

dependencies: Texture2D resources for core_texture and shard_texture
verdict: A brilliant fusion of UI and core mechanics, this system makes the silent agony of self-loss a desperate, unforgettable fight for every fragment of who you are.
impact: This invention transforms the abstract concept of identity loss into a visceral, interactive struggle. Players will constantly feel the dual pressure of external threats and internal decay, forcing split-second decisions that directly impact their sense of self. It elevates the game's core theme of 'grief of self-loss' from narrative to tangible gameplay, making every moment of danger a desperate fight not just for life, but for who Lyra *is*. The constant visual and interactive feedback ensures the player is always aware of their fading identity, deepening the emotional stakes of every encounter.
